note.question: How should strict default exclusion and record-expungement rules be, and when do graduated credit scores with differential loan rates create more repayment discipline and welfare than a simple good/bad registry?
note.overview: Borrowers privately observe project success and may default strategically, banks cannot sustain bilateral relational punishment because matching is noncommitted, and a social planner or cooperative registry chooses rating transitions and rates to make repayment incentive compatible. The paper solves constrained steady-state equilibria and optimizes the enforcement mechanism.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At the beginning of each period, every infinitely lived agent receives independent capital and productivity shocks and enters with a registry rating. Low-productivity capital holders can deposit with banks, while high-productivity agents without capital seek a one-unit loan. Banks and borrowers are randomly matched; banks follow registry rates and eligibility rules. A funded high-productivity project succeeds with probability pi and yields X or fails and yields zero.

components.label: Constrained second-best stationary lending equilibrium with incentive-compatible repayment and endogenous rating transitions
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Constrained second-best stationary lending equilibrium with incentive-compatible repayment and endogenous rating transitions. The planner chooses a registry subject to depositor participation, borrower repayment IC, bank break-even, loan-market clearing, and a constant steady-state distribution of ratings. Propositions 2-4 characterize the optimal two-tier equilibrium under sufficient and insufficient funds; Propositions 5-7 and Appendix A compare three- and N-tier stationary mechanisms.

components.label: Objective and constraints
components.explanation: The planner maximizes steady-state social welfare by maximizing funded high-productivity borrowers subject to repayment, participation, break-even, resource, and stationary-distribution constraints. Under sufficient funds, welfare is autarky welfare plus the surplus from unexcluded funded borrowers and is decreasing in registry stringency gamma/eta.
